sourcedFrom: Adams Arms Operations Manual — No edition printed (the warranty's last page carries the number 1350378.2) (UNKNOWN — no publication year is printed in the document)
cleanIntro:
This guide follows Adams Arms's operations manual for its piston rifles, which does not name the P2, so check your rifle against it. Every step below is quoted from that book and stated as generally as the book states it.

The P2 is a piston-driven AR: the gas stays at the front of the rifle, in the gas block, plug and drive rod, instead of blowing back into the receiver. So the field strip is a normal AR split — upper off the lower, bolt carrier group and charging handle out — plus the gas plug and drive rod out of the gas block. Adams Arms says most piston parts only need wiping with a dry towel, and asks for the barrel to be cleaned at least every 500 rounds.

steps.title: Selector to SAFE
steps.action: This guide follows Adams Arms's operations manual for its piston rifles, which does not name the P2, so check your rifle against it. Point the muzzle somewhere safe, keep your finger off the trigger, and turn the selector to SAFE before anything else.
steps.aside: Never allow your fingers or other objects to contact the trigger while loading or unloading the rifle.
steps.quote: Set selector to “SAFE” position.
steps.cite: Adams Arms Operations Manual — No edition printed (the warranty's last page carries the number 1350378.2) — Loading/Unloading — To Unload The Rifle, page 16 counted from the cover (the book prints no page numbers)

steps.title: Magazine out
steps.action: Press the magazine catch button and take the magazine out of the well. A round can still be in the chamber with the magazine gone, so the next step is not optional.
steps.aside: If the weapon is dropped with a loaded magazine in place, even with the bolt carrier group locked to the rear, it could chamber a round.
steps.quote: Press magazine catch button and remove magazine.
steps.cite: Adams Arms Operations Manual — No edition printed (the warranty's last page carries the number 1350378.2) — Loading/Unloading — To Unload The Rifle, page 16 counted from the cover

steps.title: Bolt locked back — chamber looked into
steps.action: Pull the charging handle to the rear and push in the lower part of the bolt catch so the bolt stays open; a chambered round is thrown clear. Then look into the chamber yourself. If you see brass, stop and clear it before going on.
steps.aside: Visually check the chamber to ensure that it is empty.
steps.quote: Pull charging handle to rear and push in lower portion of bolt catch.
steps.cite: Adams Arms Operations Manual — No edition printed (the warranty's last page carries the number 1350378.2) — Loading/Unloading — To Unload The Rifle, page 16 counted from the cover

steps.title: Bolt carrier forward, selector on SAFE
steps.action: With the rifle proven empty, let the bolt carrier group go forward and check the selector is still on SAFE. Adams Arms starts the field strip from this state.
steps.quote: Ensure the bolt carrier group is forward and the fire control selector is placed on SAFE.
steps.cite: Adams Arms Operations Manual — No edition printed (the warranty's last page carries the number 1350378.2) — Field Strip Disassembly, page 18 counted from the cover

steps.title: Rear takedown pin pushed left to right
steps.action: Push the rear takedown pin from the left side toward the right until it stops. It stays captive in the lower receiver on its detent — do not try to pull it out.
steps.quote: Press the takedown pin from left to right until it stops (It is held into the lower receiver by a detent and will not pull free from the receiver).
steps.cite: Adams Arms Operations Manual — No edition printed (the warranty's last page carries the number 1350378.2) — Field Strip Disassembly, page 18 counted from the cover

steps.title: Front pivot pin pushed left to right
steps.action: Push the front pivot pin from left to right the same way, until it stops at its detent. It also stays in the lower.
steps.quote: Press the pivot pin (front pin) from left to right until it stops at the detent.
steps.cite: Adams Arms Operations Manual — No edition printed (the warranty's last page carries the number 1350378.2) — Field Strip Disassembly, page 18 counted from the cover

steps.title: Upper lifted off the lower
steps.action: With both pins out to their stops, lift the upper receiver away from the lower receiver.
steps.quote: Separate the upper receiver from the lower receiver.
steps.cite: Adams Arms Operations Manual — No edition printed (the warranty's last page carries the number 1350378.2) — Field Strip Disassembly, page 18 counted from the cover

steps.title: Charging handle back, bolt carrier group out the rear
steps.action: Take hold of the charging handle and draw it rearward until it stops; that brings the bolt carrier group back with it. Slide the bolt carrier group out through the rear opening of the upper receiver.
steps.aside: Grasp the charging handle and pull it rearward until it stops.
steps.quote: Remove the bolt carrier group from the rear opening of the upper receiver.
steps.cite: Adams Arms Operations Manual — No edition printed (the warranty's last page carries the number 1350378.2) — Field Strip Disassembly, page 18 counted from the cover

steps.title: Charging handle out by its tabs
steps.action: Line the charging handle's tabs up with the cuts in the receiver and lift it out.
steps.quote: Align the tabs of the charging handle and lift it from the receiver.
steps.cite: Adams Arms Operations Manual — No edition printed (the warranty's last page carries the number 1350378.2) — Field Strip Disassembly, page 18 counted from the cover

steps.title: Gas plug and drive rod out of the gas block
steps.action: At the front of the rifle, press the detent button on the gas block and turn the gas plug knob to its removal position, then draw out the gas plug and the drive rod. The book shows more than one Adams Arms gas block and prints the removal position for each — 9 o'clock on the Standard block, 9 or 3 o'clock on the P Series Micro Adjustable — so check which block your rifle carries. Note your gas setting before you turn the knob, so you can return to it.
steps.aside: Then remove the drive rod and gas plug.
steps.quote: To access the drive rod for cleaning, simply press the detent button and turn the gas plug knob to the 9 o’clock position.
steps.cite: Adams Arms Operations Manual — No edition printed (the warranty's last page carries the number 1350378.2) — Cleaning/Maintaining the Piston System, page 23 counted from the cover

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Lower receiver, upper receiver, bolt carrier group, charging handle, gas plug and drive rod: that is the field strip. Adams Arms says this split lets you take the individual parts further apart for cleaning; the bolt carrier group and buffer strips are in Deep Clean.
steps.quote: This will allow you to further disassemble the individual parts of the AR for cleaning and maintenance.
steps.cite: Adams Arms Operations Manual — No edition printed (the warranty's last page carries the number 1350378.2) — Cleaning/Maintaining the Piston System, page 23 counted from the cover

steps.title: Most piston parts — wiped with a dry towel
steps.action: Because the piston keeps the hot gas out of the receiver, Adams Arms says most of the system only needs wiping off with a clean, dry towel. Wipe the outside of the drive rod and gas plug that way first.
steps.aside: The piston system keeps the hot burning gases from entering the receiver.
steps.quote: To clean most parts of our system you will simply wipe them off with a dry, clean towel.
steps.cite: Adams Arms Operations Manual — No edition printed (the warranty's last page carries the number 1350378.2) — Cleaning/Maintaining the Piston System, page 23 counted from the cover

steps.title: Gas block, plug and drive rod sleeve scrubbed
steps.action: The dirt collects in three places: the back of the gas block, the back of the gas plug, and the drive rod sleeve. Scrub those with a nylon brush or an old toothbrush and solvent.
steps.aside: The areas of the system that see the most dirt is the back of the gas block, the back of the plug, and the drive rod sleeve.
steps.quote: These parts may require some scrubbing with a nylon cleaning brush or old toothbrush and some cleaning solvent.
steps.cite: Adams Arms Operations Manual — No edition printed (the warranty's last page carries the number 1350378.2) — Cleaning/Maintaining the Piston System, page 23 counted from the cover

steps.title: Hard carbon scraped off
steps.action: Where carbon has built up and solvent will not shift it, scrape the heavy spots off with a knife, a pick or another scraping tool. Adams Arms says its melonite-treated parts stand up to this.
steps.quote: If you find an area that has a heavy build-up of carbon which will not come off with solvent, use a knife, pick, or some type of scraping tool to remove the heavy spots.
steps.cite: Adams Arms Operations Manual — No edition printed (the warranty's last page carries the number 1350378.2) — Cleaning/Maintaining the Piston System, page 23 counted from the cover

steps.title: Thin oil on the moving parts only
steps.action: Only some of the piston system wants oil: give the moving parts — the bolt carrier and the drive rod — a very thin coat, and nothing heavier. Adams Arms suggests cleaning the piston parts every 3000 rounds, or sooner if you like.
steps.aside: It is recommended to clean the piston system parts every 3000 rounds or sooner as desired.
steps.quote: Apply only a very thin coat over the moving parts (IE bold carrier and drive rod).
steps.cite: Adams Arms Operations Manual — No edition printed (the warranty's last page carries the number 1350378.2) — Cleaning/Maintaining the Piston System, page 23 counted from the cover

steps.title: Bore scrubbed with a brass brush and solvent
steps.action: Clean the barrel as you would any AR: a brass brush and the solvent of your choice through the bore. Adams Arms asks for this at least every 500 rounds.
steps.aside: It is recommended to clean the barrel at least once every 500 rounds and remaining parts as needed.
steps.quote: Normal cleanings should be done with a brass brush and your choice of solvent.
steps.cite: Adams Arms Operations Manual — No edition printed (the warranty's last page carries the number 1350378.2) — General Firearm Maintenance, page 24 counted from the cover

steps.title: Dirty solvent out with a mop or dry patches
steps.action: After brushing, take the dirty solvent and loosened fouling out with a bore mop or dry patches, then wipe the outside down with a clean, dry towel.
steps.aside: Wipe all the soiled solvent and loose particles off with a dry, clean towel.
steps.quote: Once scrubbed with a brass brush, remove soiled solvent and dirt with either a bore mop or some dry, cleaning patches.
steps.cite: Adams Arms Operations Manual — No edition printed (the warranty's last page carries the number 1350378.2) — General Firearm Maintenance, page 24 counted from the cover

steps.title: Upper parts brushed with nylon and solvent
steps.action: The rest of the upper receiver comes clean with a nylon brush and solvent.
steps.quote: The remaining parts of the upper should come clean with a nylon cleaning brush and your choice of solvent.
steps.cite: Adams Arms Operations Manual — No edition printed (the warranty's last page carries the number 1350378.2) — General Firearm Maintenance, page 24 counted from the cover

steps.title: Bolt carrier group cleaned, one drop on the bolt
steps.action: Adams Arms has the bolt carrier group taken apart for this (the strip is in Deep Clean). Clean its parts with a nylon brush and solvent, wipe them dry, and put one drop of lubricant on the outside of the bolt before the group goes back together.
steps.aside: Disassemble the bolt carrier group as shown in this owner’s manual.
steps.quote: Clean with a nylon brush and solvent, wipe dry, and apply one drop of lubrication to the outside of the bolt before re-assembling the bolt carrier group.
steps.cite: Adams Arms Operations Manual — No edition printed (the warranty's last page carries the number 1350378.2) — General Firearm Maintenance, page 24 counted from the cover

steps.title: Hammer and trigger brushed clean
steps.action: With the upper off, brush the hammer and trigger assembly in the lower with a nylon brush and solvent.
steps.aside: The lower receiver should also be cleaned and lubed regularly.
steps.quote: With the upper receiver, off of the lower clean the hammer and trigger assembly using a nylon brush and solvent.
steps.cite: Adams Arms Operations Manual — No edition printed (the warranty's last page carries the number 1350378.2) — General Firearm Maintenance, page 24 counted from the cover

steps.title: Action wiped, a drop on the moving parts
steps.action: Wipe the dirty solvent and loose grit out of the action, then put a drop of lubricant on the moving parts.
steps.quote: Wipe soiled solvent and loose material from the action and apply a drop of lubrication to the moving parts.
steps.cite: Adams Arms Operations Manual — No edition printed (the warranty's last page carries the number 1350378.2) — General Firearm Maintenance, page 24 counted from the cover

deepSteps.title: Firing pin retaining pin out of the left side
deepSteps.action: With the bolt carrier group out of the rifle, take the firing pin retaining pin out of the left side of the bolt carrier. A small punch may be needed to start it.
deepSteps.aside: A small punch might be needed for this procedure.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the firing pin retaining pin from the left side of the bolt carrier.
deepSteps.cite: Adams Arms Operations Manual — No edition printed (the warranty's last page carries the number 1350378.2) — Disassembly of Bolt Carrier Group, page 20 counted from the cover

deepSteps.title: Carrier tilted up, firing pin caught
deepSteps.action: Tip the front of the bolt carrier up and catch the firing pin as it slides out of the back of the bolt — do not let it drop.
deepSteps.quote: Tilt the bolt carrier upward and catch the firing pin as it slides out of the rear of the bolt.
deepSteps.cite: Adams Arms Operations Manual — No edition printed (the warranty's last page carries the number 1350378.2) — Disassembly of Bolt Carrier Group, page 20 counted from the cover

deepSteps.title: Cam pin turned a quarter and lifted out
deepSteps.action: Turn the bolt cam pin a quarter turn and lift it straight up out of the carrier. Adams Arms warns that a rifle reassembled without its cam pin can still fire and will blow up — so when the group goes back together, the cam pin goes back in.
deepSteps.aside: Be sure the cam pin is installed in the bolt group.
deepSteps.quote: Rotate the bolt cam pin ¼ turn and lift it straight up out of the bolt carrier.
deepSteps.cite: Adams Arms Operations Manual — No edition printed (the warranty's last page carries the number 1350378.2) — Disassembly of Bolt Carrier Group, page 20 counted from the cover

deepSteps.title: Bolt out the front of the carrier
deepSteps.action: Draw the bolt forward and out of the front of the bolt carrier.
deepSteps.quote: Pull the bolt out from the front of the bolt carrier.
deepSteps.cite: Adams Arms Operations Manual — No edition printed (the warranty's last page carries the number 1350378.2) — Disassembly of Bolt Carrier Group, page 20 counted from the cover

deepSteps.title: Thumb on the back of the extractor
deepSteps.action: Press lightly on the rear of the extractor with your thumb, which takes its spring's load off the pin.
deepSteps.quote: Apply slight pressure to the rear of the extractor with the thumb.
deepSteps.cite: Adams Arms Operations Manual — No edition printed (the warranty's last page carries the number 1350378.2) — Extractor Removal, page 21 counted from the cover

deepSteps.title: Extractor pin pushed out
deepSteps.action: Keeping that pressure on, push the extractor pin out from either side with a punch or the tip of the firing pin.
deepSteps.quote: Using a punch, or the tip of the firing pin, push out the extractor pin.
deepSteps.cite: Adams Arms Operations Manual — No edition printed (the warranty's last page carries the number 1350378.2) — Extractor Removal, page 21 counted from the cover

deepSteps.title: Extractor off the bolt — spring left in it
deepSteps.action: Lift the extractor off the bolt. Leave its spring in place: Adams Arms says to separate the spring from the extractor only when it is being replaced.
deepSteps.aside: Only separate the extractor spring from the extractor when replacement is necessary
deepSteps.quote: Remove the extractor from the bolt.
deepSteps.cite: Adams Arms Operations Manual — No edition printed (the warranty's last page carries the number 1350378.2) — Extractor Removal, page 21 counted from the cover

deepSteps.title: Buffer retainer pressed, buffer eased forward
deepSteps.action: Wear safety glasses — this part is under spring tension. The buffer comes out more easily with the hammer cocked and the selector on SAFE. Press the buffer retaining plunger and keep a thumb on the buffer as the spring pushes it forward out of the receiver extension.
deepSteps.aside: ALWAYS WEAR SAFETY GLASSES WHEN HANDLING PARTS UNDER SPRING TENSION.
deepSteps.quote: Depress buffer retaining plunger while maintaining control the buffer as you allow it to move forward from the receiver extension tube.
deepSteps.cite: Adams Arms Operations Manual — No edition printed (the warranty's last page carries the number 1350378.2) — Removal of Buffer and Buffer Spring, page 22 counted from the cover

deepSteps.title: Buffer and action spring guided out
deepSteps.action: Guide the buffer and the action spring out of the receiver extension.
deepSteps.quote: Guide the buffer and action spring from the receiver extension.
deepSteps.cite: Adams Arms Operations Manual — No edition printed (the warranty's last page carries the number 1350378.2) — Removal of Buffer and Buffer Spring, page 22 counted from the cover

deepSteps.title: Spring twisted off the buffer — never pulled
deepSteps.action: To part the spring from the buffer, twist it clockwise off the buffer. Do not pull the spring straight back: stretching it changes how it works. This is the last strip the book publishes.
deepSteps.aside: DO NOT pull straight back on the action spring as any stretching will affect the function of the spring.
deepSteps.quote: Use a clockwise twisting motion to separate the action spring from the recoil buffer.
deepSteps.cite: Adams Arms Operations Manual — No edition printed (the warranty's last page carries the number 1350378.2) — Removal of Buffer and Buffer Spring, page 22 counted from the cover

cleaning.name: PISTON SYSTEM
tasks: Gas plug and drive rod out of the gas block
Most parts wiped with a dry, clean towel
Back of the gas block, back of the plug and the drive rod sleeve scrubbed with a nylon brush and solvent
Hard carbon scraped off the heavy spots
Only a very thin coat of oil, on the moving parts
Drive rod and plug back in; gas setting returned to where it was

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: Brass brush and solvent through the bore
Dirty solvent out with a bore mop or dry patches
Outside wiped with a dry, clean towel

cleaning.name: UPPER & BOLT CARRIER
tasks: Upper parts brushed with a nylon brush and solvent
Bolt carrier group parts cleaned and wiped dry
One drop of lubricant on the outside of the bolt
Do not reassemble the bolt carrier group without its cam pin

cleaning.name: LOWER RECEIVER
tasks: Hammer and trigger assembly brushed with a nylon brush and solvent
Soiled solvent and loose material wiped out of the action
A drop of lubricant on the moving parts

reassembly: Bolt carrier group back together if it was stripped — bolt in from the front, cam pin in and turned, firing pin in, retaining pin in from the left. The cam pin must be in.
Action spring and buffer back into the receiver extension past the retaining plunger, if they were out.
Drive rod and gas plug back into the gas block at the removal position; press the detent button and turn the plug to your gas setting.
Charging handle into the upper by its tabs, bolt carrier group in behind it, both pushed home.
Upper back on the lower, pivot pin and takedown pin pushed home; lock the action back, check the rifle is empty, selector on SAFE, then a function check before any ammunition.
fncheck: Adams Arms asks for a function check after every cleaning and reassembly, with the rifle cleared. Insert an unloaded magazine, pull the charging handle fully back until the bolt locks open, push the handle forward, and put the selector on SAFE. Press the magazine catch: the magazine should fall free. Press the bolt catch: the bolt should go forward. Pull the trigger on SAFE: the hammer should not fall. Turn the selector to SEMI and pull the trigger, holding it back: the hammer should fall. Still holding the trigger, pull the charging handle fully back to recock, then let the trigger out slowly: you should hear a click. If any of these fails, the rifle is not used until it is put right.
